Firefoux Dungeon.mechanics:
thumb|300px|Firefoux Dungeon Rooms
 isn't arranged like a normal dungeon (in that you kill a mob to progress to the next room), instead it is an open arrangement of 8 maps, shown in the map to the right.

In order to progress through the dungeon and fight Peki Peki in the final room, you must first acquire the 6 Firefacts. These are Quest Items unique to the dungeon, which you drop from a Zilla. In each of the dungeon's 6 main rooms there is a Zilla and each Zilla drops a unique Firefact, ranging from First Firefact to Sixth Firefact. Once you have obtained all of the Firefacts you may go to the last room, which upon entering you lose all 6 Firefacts and the Firefoux Dungeon Key.

Inner Labyrinth of the Minotoror.mechanics:
In order to pass through the dungeon players must obtain a Mumminotor Relic and a Deminoball Relic. These are dropped by the Mumminotor and Deminoball respectively, which spawn in any of the rooms 1 to 25, but not room 13.

Players enter in the unlabeled room on the map below. In the maze most of the doors are closed (except the doors to room 1, 2 and 6 which are always open). In order to open them players must pull levers found in the rooms. A lever in one room opens the doors in the room next to it, but also closes the door next to the lever.

650px

To open the doors, it is recommended to do this with at least two players. Following the below image, P1 should follow the outside ring (red path) going down from room 1 to 2 etc., and P2 should follow the inside ring (blue path) going from room 1 to 6 and then down to 7 etc. Shown are the levers in every room connected to the right door that needs to be opened to let players through. Doing this strategy will take players through the whole labyrinth except room 13, which doesn't have any monsters. This could also be done clockwise rather than counter clockwise, but the text instructions will be counter-clockwise.

650px

Lord Crow's Library.mechanics:
thumb|400px
You need to find and kill Foxo the Crowfox, Horace the Tamed Crobak and Kapotie the Drinker. They usually spawn separately. Each one you kill will give you the corresponding feather as an alteration.

You can walk freely between rooms, without the need to kill any other mobs. Once you have killed the 3 "library keepers", go back and talk to Virgil to enter the dungeon proper (consisting of 2 rooms), which consumes the key.

Pet Sanctuary.mechanics:
differs from other dungeons as in it your characters are all transformed into one of four Pet Ghost types, and must fight other Pet Ghosts to progress.

You have the choice of which Ghost to fight as at the start of the dungeon. The four choices are:
* Bow Meow Ghost: 110 HP. Melee warrior, may attack twice a turn, add MP or agility and has a weak ranged spell.
* Gobtubby Ghost: 120 HP. Tank, has a moderate earth melee spell, can shield itself and an ally, can also attract a target.
* Pandawa Cub Ghost: 100 HP. A healer. Has a weak ranged attack, two healing spells (one AoE, one single target) and can unbewitch a target.
* Pink Dragoone Ghost: 90 HP. Distance fighter, can pushback a target, remove range and MP.

You also encounter the following enemies:
* Crobak Ghost: 80 HP, ranged fighter.
* Bilby Ghost: 90 HP, can remove MP and ranged attack.
* Bworky Ghost: 120 HP, tank.
* Crocodyl Ghost: 125 HP, AoE ranged fighter.
* Croum Ghost: 120 HP, tank.
* El Scarador Ghost: 80 HP, healer, AoE ranged fighter.
* Leopardo Ghost: 80 HP, close combat fighter can remove MP.
* Ross Ghost: 70 HP, healer.
* Treechster Ghost: 90 HP, can remove AP and deal ranged damage in an AoE.
* Willy Peninzias: 70 HP, close combat fighter can remove MP.
* Young Wild Boar Ghost: 90 HP, removes AP.

The Jellith Dimension.mechanics:
works somewhat differently to other dungeons. In each room you are faced with 4 mobs (and so must choose one of the following mobs listed on this page). Each mob of Jellies killed drops a Quest Item called a Pool of Jelly. You will get a Pool of Jelly based on the type of Jelly most dominating the mob, so fighting 4 Strawberry Jellies, 2 Mint Jellies, 1 Blue Jelly and 1 Lemon Jelly  would drop a Pool of Strawberry Jelly.

The boss mob, fought in the 5th room, depends upon which Pools of Jelly you have collected in the dungeon. Upon entering the 5th room you will see the 4 Royal Jellies playing a game; talking to either of the Royal Jellies will teleport you into another room with the boss mob. If you have each of the 4 colored Pools, talking to the Royal Jellies will teleport you into a room whereby you can fight all 4 Royal Jellies in a singular fight. If you are missing one of the Pools, you will be teleported into a room with the Royal Jelly corresponding to the pool you have the greatest amount of.

Count Razof's Camp.mechanics:
When the fight starts, Count Razof has almost 100% resistance on all elements. You reduce it by 20% per each summon your team has alive. He also summons a Minikron, a little pink unicorn that follows the character that summoned it around. When it finishes close to you, it heals and shields you for aprox. 8% of your max health. I recommend you lock it with a high lock character, kill the rest of the mob and then take care of the summons.
For achievements duo Cra and Panda worked just fine with Panda tanking it and Cra finishing the mob from afar.
At the end of his turn, Razof will lose 20% resistance per each summon your group controls that is alive (except for static summons). If the count kills a player his resistance to the element of his current sate will be reduced by 20% for 10 turns.

Kolosso's Caverns.mechanics:
Unlike most other dungeons, progress in the  is not linear. Upon entering the dungeon players are greeted with five doors, four of which are numbered one, two, four and five, and the fifth with Professor Xa (NPC) next to it. (Another room with the number three used to be available, but was removed in order to shorten the dungeon.)

The numbered doors lead to rooms (called Badgette, Badgom, Badgauve and Jewel respectively) containing a mob each.

In order to enter the room by Professor Xa (NPC), which contains the final boss mob, players need to have the four relics. These relics are dropped by the mobs within each of the numbered rooms. Each of the rooms contains a unique relic. Players can collect up to five of each relic (after which point they cannot enter back into the numbered rooms) though only need one complete set in order to pass by Professor Xa. The rooms can be done in any order.

Bzzegg Supervisor starts the fight invulnerable. To remove the invulnerability, you must hit the boss four times with an explosion from killing one of the monsters summoned eggs. Once Bzzegg Supervisor become vulnerable, he gains +20% Critical Hit and +10% Final Damage for the rest of the fight. He will also unbewitch Gravity state immediately on his turn. When Bzzegg Supervisor summons a clone of himself, the clone will explode in two turns dealing 500 fire damage to everyone within 3 range of him. If you kill the summoned clone before it explodes, Bzzegg Supervisor will take 20% additional damage for one turn. Bzzegg Supervisor teleports to the closest player character at the start of his turn, and when Bzzegg Supervisor is eventually killed, he will deal 250 damage in all elements to everyone within 3 range of him.

Fouxwork Factory.mechanics:
In the final room, all monsters start out invulnerable. The boss will summon torches and some barrels first turn. To make the monsters vulnerable you need to extinguish all the torches. You need to extinguish at least one of the torches before the second turn. If all the torches are lit after the first turn, everyone on the team will be instantly killed. This applies to any turn afterwards, not just the second turn; if all torches are lit when Founoroshi starts his turn your team will be instantly killed.

To extinguish a torch, a character needs to stand on one of the blue glyphs placed by the boss and then afterwards run and stand on the brown glyph next to the torch. Extinguishing a torch gives you a -10% resistance debuff for 4 turns and also buffs the boss. Torches will light again after 7 turns of being extinguished. The barrels will heal and shield you if you hit them. Upon being hit, the barrel will also pull you in if you are not next to it, or push you away if you are next to it.
Fouxwork Factory.notes: The Founoroshi fight cannot be souled.

Grozilla and Grasmera's Den.mechanics:
No matter which version of Grozilla and Grasmera the players want to face, they will have to pass through 2 rooms in Nomads' Land with 5 Sauroshells of different colours in each room before directly reaching .
There are 4 types of the rooms filled with 4 different Sauroshell level groups for 4 different character level categories. Each player can only access one type of the rooms of its own level category.
thumb|center|450px|There are 4 types of the rooms for different level categories
#Levels 1-50 --> can only enter "Tourist Room" and access 2 rooms consisting of 5 different Juvenile Sauroshells
#Levels 51-100 --> can only enter "Amateur Room" and access 2 rooms consisting of 5 different Novice Sauroshells
#Levels 101-150 --> can only enter "Specialist Room" and access 2 rooms consisting of 5 different Mature Sauroshells
#Levels 151-200 --> can only enter "Expert Room" and access 2 rooms consisting of 5 different Venerable Sauroshells
So, for example, level 151 and level 200 characters can go through Nomads' Land together, but level 150 and level 151 characters will have to beat the rooms separately before meeting each other at the entrance of .

Shogun Tofugawa's Tomb.mechanics:
You will need the spell Slayspirit Lantern which can be obtained by trading 4 Samurai Ghost Fabric with Danaba Retzu. The boss starts invulnerable and to vuln him you need to cast the spell when he is within range, making him suffer pushback damage. Casting the spell on yourself will activate the lantern and also push monsters next to you 3(?) cells away.

Making the Shogun vulnerable places a glyph throughout the room where the enemy monsters are invisible, unless they are within the lantern glyph. The invisibility glyph is active for the duration of the Shogun's vulnerability.  When becoming vulneralbe Shogun will summon two assisins with 3100 vit, they don't do much damage.  If you don't kill Shogon in a single turn there is a 2 or 3 turn cool down before Shogun can become vulnerable again.

The Venerable One's Thicket.key: Key to the Venerable One's Thicket
The Venerable One's Thicket.mechanics:
All monsters start in the apathetic state, meaning that they have 80% reduced stats, and 1 MP (depending on the season), and generally won't attack or will deal low damage due to their reduced stats. When a monster is hit, it leaves the apathetic state and enters the alerted state for two turns, removes the reduced stats, and alerts all monsters within 3 range at the time the monster is hit. This can cause a chain reaction for monsters are within 3 range of a monster that was just alerted, even if they are not within 3 range of the initial monster that was alerted. Every time a monster is hit not through damage sharing, the alerted state is refreshed for two turns, but if the monster is not hit for two turns it will go back into the apathetic state.

The boss starts off the fight invulnerable, -100 MP, and just passes his turn. This is his apathetic state. The boss can be alerted just like the rest of the monsters, and will go back to apathetic state like normal, or you can kill his summon which will remove his apathetic state permanently.

Turtelonia's Sanctuary.mechanics:
In this dungeon, all monsters have a special mechanic called "lunar cycle". Thus each turn, all the monsters of the fight gain a bonus according to the cycle.
;  Killing a monster during one of these cycles will give the bonus of the current cycle to all monsters for the rest of the fight!
The cycles start in this order and once a cycle is finished, we go back to the beginning of the cycle and it's a loop:
# File:New Moon.png New Moon: When you hit a monster a light damage return is applied to the allies in a radius 2 radius area around you. If you kill a monster, all the others have a reconstitution + the invulnerable state (1 turn).
# File:Waxing Crescent.png Waxing Crescent: Damage suffered x80%.
# File:First Quarter.png First Quarter: 10% Resistance.
# File:Waxing Gibbous.png Waxing Gibbous: 2 MP.
# File:Full Moon.png Full Moon: Damage returned by 200%.
# File:Waning Gibbous.png Waning Gibbous: 2 AP.
# File:Last Quarter.png Last Quarter: 500 SP.
# File:Waning Crescent.png Waning Crescent: Increases final damage caused by 20%.
;  Avoid killing monsters during the Full Moon state (most important), and New Moon.

Wind Dojo.mechanics: The final room has two bosses, Hanshi and Shihan.  They share all dmg with over 10K vit between them.  One achievement is to kill Hanshi last. For this achievement, knowing that Hanshi and Shihan share their damage and that Hanshi reduces melee damage by 50% while Shihan reduces ranged damage by 50%, it is better to rush Shihan in melee, causing Shihan to die first.
